descriptionChirho: The proper name Kalev (כָּלֵב), primarily referring to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan and one of only two (with Joshua) who brought a faithful report and were permitted to enter the Promised Land (Num 13-14, 26:65, 32:12; Deut 1:36; Josh 14:6-14, 15:13-19; Judg 1:12-20; 1 Sam 25:3, 30:14; 1 Chr 4:15, 6:56). Also used for Caleb son of Hezron (1 Chr 2:18,42,46,48-50). English renders as Caleb/Kalev; Spanish Caleb/Kalev; Hindi कालेब (Kaaleb); Arabic كالِب (Kalib); Korean 갈렙/갈렛 (Gallep/Gallet); Swahili Kalebu. Both clusters refer to the same individual(s) — the second adds conjunctive and prepositional prefixes (and-Caleb, to-Caleb) without semantic distinction.
